Let \(b\ge 2\) be an integer. Call a positive integer \(n\) \(b\text-\textit{eautiful}\) if it has exactly two digits when expressed in base \(b\)  and these two digits sum to \(\sqrt n\). For example, \(81\) is \(13\text-\textit{eautiful}\) because \(81  = \underline{6} \ \underline{3}_{13} \) and \(6 + 3 =  \sqrt{81}\). Find the least integer \(b\ge 2\) for which there are more than ten \(b\text-\textit{eautiful}\) integers.assistant

Step 4: Realize that the largest possible sum of two digits in base b is b-1, since the largest digit in base b is b-1. Therefore, the largest possible sum of two digits that can be equal to √n is b-1.

Step 10: Since we found more than ten b-eautiful numbers for b = 4, we can stop here and conclude that the least integer b ≥ 2 for which there are more than ten b-eautiful integers is 4.
